summary.title: Einstein vs Maxwell: Is gravitation a curvature of space, a field in flat space, or both?
summary.executive_summary: This paper proposes a field-theoretic formulation of General Relativity (GTR) within a fixed Minkowski background, deriving a proper gravitational energy-momentum tensor that cancels material energy in flat cosmology. The author extends this to the Relativistic Theory of Gravitation (RTG), a bimetric theory breaking general coordinate invariance. This extension regularizes the Schwarzschild black hole interior, preventing singularities and allowing escape, while maintaining agreement with solar system tests. In cosmology, the theory naturally recovers the ΛCDM model, predicts early inflation, and ensures total energy vanishes by canceling vacuum and zero-point energies. The work concludes that while GTR and field theory are equivalent, the bimetric extension supports viewing gravity as a field in flat space (Maxwell's view).

The bimetric theory regularizes the Schwarzschild black hole interior.
The theory naturally incorporates the ΛCDM cosmological model.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper proposes a field-theoretic formulation of General Relativity (GTR) within a fixed Minkowski background, deriving a proper gravitational energy-momentum tensor that cancels material energy in flat cosmology. The author extends this to the Relativistic Theory of Gravitation (RTG), a bimetric theory breaking general coordinate invariance. This extension regularizes the Schwarzschild black hole interior, preventing singularities and allowing escape, while maintaining agreement with solar system tests. In cosmology, the theory naturally recovers the ΛCDM model, predicts early inflation, and ensures total energy vanishes by canceling vacuum and zero-point energies. The work concludes that while GTR and field theory are equivalent, the bimetric extension supports viewing gravity as a field in flat space (Maxwell's view).

Research Context
Einstein moved from flat to curved space via general coordinates. A fundamental difficulty is how to deal with the physics of gravitation itself. There is only a quasi energy-momentum tensor in standard GTR. Energy transfer from waves to detectors remains an open question. The proper energy momentum tensor was derived recently by Babak and Grishchuk. Nathan Rosen considers a bimetric theory involving Minkowski and Riemann metrics.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The paper asks if gravitation is curvature, a field, or both. The hypothesis is that a field theoretic approach in Minkowski space yields a proper tensor. It is hypothesized that gravitational energy is negative and cancels material energy. The bimetric coupling breaks general coordinate invariance. A singularity-free Schwarzschild solution is predicted in the interior. The theory should cover the ΛCDM model and allow early inflation.

Methodological Details
The study starts with a field theoretic approach in Minkowski space. The Minkowski metric is defined as ηµν = diag(1, −1, −1, −1). The Riemann metric is defined by rg γ gµν = γµν + hµν. Christoffel symbols are replaced by Minkowski covariant ones. The acceleration tensor is defined as Aµν = 1/2 DαDβ(kµνkαβ −kµαkνβ). The total energy momentum tensor is Θµν = g/γ θµν. Cosmology is described by the Friedman-Lemaitre-Robertson-Walker metric. Flat space is considered with k = 0 and U = 1. The Relativistic Theory of Gravitation uses a bimetric coupling. The cosmological constant is set to ρΛ = ρbi.

Procedures And Architectures
The gravitational action is expressed in terms of Minkowski covariant derivatives. Three extra terms are added to the Lagrangian involving gauge transformations. The bimetric term acts like a mass term breaking coordinate invariance. The Einstein equations couple the Riemann metric to matter. The harmonic condition Dνhµν = 0 is imposed automatically. The Schwarzschild solution is scaled by rh = GM/c². A parametric solution is found for the black hole interior functions. The scale factor a(t) is used to describe cosmic expansion. The modified Friedman equation includes Λbi terms. The theory predicts exponential growth at large times.

Key Results
The total energy density is zero in flat space cosmology. Gravitational energy density is negative and cancels matter energy. The graviton has an imaginary mass in this theory. Gravitational waves are unstable at the Hubble scale. The horizon radius equals half the Schwarzschild radius. The dimensionless parameter is ¯λ = 2.38 × 10⁻²³ M/M⊙. Inside the horizon, U and V decay rapidly but remain positive. The transition layer width is ℓ* = ηrh. The time to hit the center is T = 2.74 × 10³² M/M⊙ yr. The theory recovers the ΛCDM model at large times. The scale factor grows as a = C exp(H∞τ). The vacuum energy vanishes due to cancellation.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
Curvature is a geometric description of the gravitational field in flat space. Clusters of galaxies do not move away from each other in time. The speed of light changes with cosmic time, dr/dt = [a(t)/a*]²c. The quantum version will involve quantization of fields, not space. Both curved space and field views apply to the same physics. The bimetric extension supports viewing gravity as a field in flat space.

Contradictions And Limitations
True black holes with horizons do not occur if ρΛ, ρbi → 0. The theory has self-repulsive properties for matter falling onto a black hole. There is a minimal and a maximal size of the scale factor. The approach makes sense only for M > 10³ M⊙. The Logunov case has ¯µ² < 0 leading to w′ < 0. The theory does not allow a solution with u′(0) = 0 for α < 0.

Claims
The proper gravitational energy-momentum tensor exists and cancels material energy. The tensor is conserved, DνΘµν = 0. Total energy density is zero in flat cosmology. Standard GTR has only a quasi tensor. Energy transfer from waves to detectors is clarified.
The bimetric theory regularizes the Schwarzschild black hole interior. Components die out but do not change sign. Time keeps its role as usual in the interior. Logunov theory has self-repulsive properties. Escape is, in principle, possible from the interior.
The theory naturally incorporates the ΛCDM cosmological model. The model gives the best fit of observations. There is a form of inflation at early times. The cosmological constant is finite and positive. Zero point energy vanishes in this framework.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Solar system effects are reproduced for small ρΛ terms. Differences arise only for large gravitational fields.
